oracle_provenance: Independent inverse-variance/circular-mean worked examples (standard scalar Kalman-filter-style fusion applied through unit-vector angle averaging); not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded two-source circular fusion of an IMU heading and an acoustic DOA estimate; not physical bench-verified sensor fusion.

cases.question: Does a more-precise IMU heading and a less-precise acoustic DOA fuse to a value closer to the IMU, with correctly reduced uncertainty?
Across the 0/360 degree wrap boundary (350 vs 10 degrees, a true 20-degree difference), does the circular fusion avoid the naive-average error of treating this as a 340-degree difference?
Must a zero (or negative) declared angular standard deviation be rejected rather than producing an infinite inverse-variance weight?
When the two sources disagree by nearly 180 degrees, is that flagged as a possible sign/frame-convention error rather than fused into a falsely confident middle value?
When the two sensors' timestamps are far apart relative to the declared tolerance, is the fusion flagged as unreliable due to skew even though the angles themselves agree well?
